content.thinking: I'm changing "from" to "over" in those phrases, since the figures are ranges and "from" implies a starting point. That applies to the account page sentence, step 2's "in the minute" wording, and step 3.

action_items.item: Require passing tests of a feature flag's on path, including accounts with no purchases in the current period, before the flag can be switched on in production for io-shop.
Roll out io-shop feature flags to a small share of traffic first, and widen them only while the error rate stays at its usual level.
Switch a feature flag off automatically when the io-shop error rate rises during its rollout.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to the on-call rota, so that it pages a person.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The service's own warning on the account page error rate climbed from its usual level to its highest at {Gbac1.7}, and failed account page requests were logged over {G5309.3}.
The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError: division by zero in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, at line {F1.1}. This was logged over {G5309.3} and again at {G5309.6}, and not before.

That code ran because the service had started evaluating monthly-spend-feature as on. Before the onset, every evaluation read it as off and account pages rendered normally. In the minute {G971b.6} some evaluations read it as on, and over {Gce95.4} every evaluation did.

ruled_out.what: A deploy: the production change events read on both passes held only flag changes, and no deploy came back.

causal_chain.step: The service evaluated the flag as on because an admin switched monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}.

Turning the flag on broke the service because the spend-summary path it enables divides by the number of purchases a shopper made this month, which is zero for shoppers who have not bought anything this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Someone switched on a new monthly spending summary for shoppers' account pages, and the code behind it likely divides by the number of things a shopper bought this month, which breaks the page for shoppers who have not bought anything yet this month.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that exercised the code path monthly-spend-feature enables, such as a shopper with no purchases this month, before the flag was switched on in production.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have been found before the flag reached shoppers, and the flag would not have been switched on with the fault in place.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went to all of the service's traffic almost at once. Some evaluations read it as on in its first minute, and every evaluation did from the next minute. No gradual rollout or automatic stop was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers would have reached the failing path, and the rollout could have been stopped once the error rate rose.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been brought in to switch the flag off and confirm the service took the change, instead of the service being left failing with the flag on.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident in the same minute the flag was switched on.
The Mitigation Agent reverted monthly-spend-feature, the change the evidence pointed to, and the revert can be undone.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix for the failing line as a draft pull request for a person to review.

went_wrong: The Mitigation Agent judged the flag revert refuted while the service's own log still showed every evaluation reading monthly-spend-feature as on at {Gce95.7}, after the revert. The revert was judged without anyone seeing the service take it. The flag was then put back on, and the second investigation came back with the same candidate.

input.root_cause: In src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, `average_spend_per_item_this_month`, which `render_spend_summary` reaches only when `use_monthly_summary` is true and `use_typical_spend` is false (the path monthly-spend-feature turns on), divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of purchases made this month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that number is zero, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1}, and the error reaches the account page and fails the request.
input.still_at_risk: Account pages could keep failing for shoppers as long as monthly-spend-feature stays on, and the same failure could come back any time the flag is switched on before the fault is fixed.
input.stops_the_harm: Switch monthly-spend-feature off again. Confirm at the service that its flag-evaluation log reads monthly-spend-feature=off for every evaluation, that the ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py stops, and that the account page error rate falls back to its level before the onset.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
input.why_it_did_not_help: Find out whether the revert of monthly-spend-feature reached the service, since the service's log still showed the flag evaluated as on at {Gce95.7}, after the revert. If it did reach the service, find out why account page requests kept failing with ZeroDivisionError.
